resources.title: Harmonization in magnetic resonance imaging: A survey of acquisition, image-level, and feature-level methods
resources.note: The broadest map of the field: covers prospective (acquisition and vendor-neutral sequences) as well as retrospective image- and feature-level harmonization, with traveling-subject resources. Start here if you need the big picture.

resources.title: Deep learning for the harmonization of structural MRI scans: a survey
resources.note: Organises deep-learning harmonization of structural MRI by architecture (U-Net, GANs, VAEs, flows, transformers), supervision (paired vs unpaired) and output, and lists the datasets and metrics used to evaluate them.

resources.title: An overview of disentangled representation learning for MR image harmonization
resources.venue: Deep Learning for Medical Image Analysis (2nd ed.), Elsevier — book chapter
resources.note: Short, focused explanation of why anatomy/contrast disentanglement works for MR harmonization, from the group behind CALAMITI and HACA3. Read it to understand that whole family of image-level methods.

resources.title: Cross–scanner harmonization methods for structural MRI may need further work: A comparison study
resources.note: Head-to-head test on GE/Siemens crossover and longitudinal participants of neural style transfer, CycleGAN, conditional GAN, histogram matching, ComBat and LongComBat for cortical thickness. A sobering read on how much is left to fix.

resources.title: Machine Learning for Brain MRI Data Harmonisation: A Systematic Review
resources.note: PRISMA review of 41 studies. Its split between explicit harmonization (produce harmonized data) and implicit harmonization (make the downstream model site-invariant, e.g. domain adaptation) is a useful lens when choosing a method.

resources.title: Harmonization Strategies in Multicenter MRI-Based Radiomics
resources.note: Practical guide for radiomics pipelines: what to do at image level (bias-field correction, intensity normalization, resampling, GAN-based standardization) and at feature level (ComBat and variants), and where each step fits.

resources.title: Site effects how-to and when: An overview of retrospective techniques to accommodate site effects in multi-site neuroimaging analyses
resources.note: The most practical decision guide for feature-level work: when a mixed-effects model is enough, when to use ComBat or a variant, IQM-based adjustment, normative modeling or deep learning, with benefits and drawbacks for each use case.

resources.title: Impact of leakage on data harmonization in machine learning pipelines in class imbalance across sites
resources.note: Shows that when class labels are imbalanced across sites, ComBat-based harmonization only helps a classifier if it is given the test labels — that is, through leakage. Without them it removes the signal of interest. Essential before putting any ComBat-family method into an ML pipeline; introduces PrettYharmonize as a leakage-free alternative.

resources.title: Image harmonization: A review of statistical and deep learning methods for removing batch effects and evaluation metrics for effective harmonization
resources.note: Broad review of statistical and deep-learning image harmonization for MRI and CT, with a clear taxonomy (intensity normalization, ComBat-style models, image translation, disentanglement) and a discussion of how to evaluate them.

resources.title: Making Radiomics More Reproducible across Scanner and Imaging Protocol Variations: A Review of Harmonization Methods
resources.note: Radiomics-focused review of how scanner, protocol and reconstruction settings change radiomic features, and of the image- and feature-level fixes proposed for it.

resources.title: Harmonization strategies for multicenter radiomics investigations
resources.note: Classic overview of harmonization strategies for multicenter radiomics: acquisition standardization, image post-processing, feature selection and ComBat-style feature correction.

resources.title: Harmonization of Brain Diffusion MRI: Concepts and Methods
resources.note: Concepts-first review of diffusion MRI harmonization: sources of variability, signal-level (RISH, deep learning) versus feature-level (ComBat) methods, and traveling-subject challenges.

resources.title: A General Primer for Data Harmonization
resources.note: Not imaging-specific: harmonization in the data-integration sense (making variables from different surveys or studies comparable). Useful background on terminology and planning; it does not cover scanner effects.

resources.title: Challenges and best practices when using ComBAT to harmonize diffusion MRI data
resources.note: Practical guide to ComBat for diffusion MRI: the model's assumptions, what happens when they are violated (small sites, unbalanced covariates, non-linear age effects), and recommendations. Read before running ComBat on clinical dMRI data.

resources.title: Potential and Limitations of ComBat for the Harmonization of Multi-Site Neuroimaging Studies
resources.note: Tests ComBat beyond scanner effects (e.g. differences in segmentation software) with direct rather than indirect success measures, showing where it helps and where it does not.

resources.title: Quantitative Metrics for Benchmarking Medical Image Harmonization
resources.note: Proposes three metrics for benchmarking image harmonization without ground truth: two for intensity harmonization and one for anatomy preservation. Handy when you have no traveling subjects.

resources.title: Harmonization techniques for machine learning studies using multi-site functional MRI data
resources.note: Compares harmonization techniques for machine-learning studies on multi-site resting-state fMRI (connectivity features), including the effect on downstream classification of psychiatric disorders.

resources.title: Comparison of Multi-site Neuroimaging Data Harmonization Techniques for Machine Learning Applications
resources.note: Short comparison of multi-site harmonization techniques in a machine-learning context: how well each removes site information and what it does to predictive performance.

resources.title: Evaluation of Image‐Level Harmonization Methods for Multi‐Center MR Neuroimaging
authors: the Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration Neuroimaging Initiative
resources.note: Evaluates scanner differences in ADNI T1w and T2-FLAIR images and benchmarks image-level harmonization methods (including CALAMITI, HACA3 and ComBat-style baselines) on them.

resources.title: Evaluating MRI harmonisation methods with multicentre data from the Psy-ShareD consortium: A comparative analysis
resources.note: Evaluates MRI harmonisation methods on multicentre T1w data from the Psy-ShareD consortium, separating removal of scanner variance from preservation of biological signal (age, sex).

resources.title: Harmonizing multicenter quantitative imaging data: sources of variability, statistical solutions, and practical workflows in CT and MRI
resources.note: Review for epidemiologists: sources of variability in multicenter MRI, CT and PET-CT, their impact on inference (misclassification, lost power) and the statistical and AI-based harmonization options.

resources.title: Harmonising Structural Brain MRI from Multiple Sites with Limited Sample Sizes
resources.note: Systematic evaluation of image-based and statistical harmonisation on a small multisite, multiscanner T1w test-retest dataset (repeatability, intra- and inter-scanner reproducibility), using metrics for both technical and biological variability. Relevant when you have few subjects per site.

resources.title: ComBat models for harmonization of resting-state EEG features in multisite studies
resources.note: Compares four ComBat variants (neuroCombat, ComBat-GAM, OPNested ComBat-GMM, HarmonizR) on oscillatory and aperiodic resting-state EEG features pooled from five datasets (n = 374); OPNested-GMM and HarmonizR removed batch effects best while keeping age relationships.

resources.title: Multi-site harmonization for magnetoencephalography spectral power data
resources.note: Tests ComBat, ComBat-GAM, CovBat (GAM) and RELIEF on MEG spectral power from 16 open datasets recorded on different MEG platforms; ComBat-GAM was the best choice for removing site effects while keeping nonlinear age effects.

resources.title: A Guide to ComBat Harmonization of Imaging Biomarkers in Multicenter Studies
resources.note: Practical guide to ComBat for imaging biomarkers (SUVs, radiomic features): how to apply it on worked examples, and the situations where its assumptions are not met and it should not be used.

resources.title: MAGNIMS recommendations for harmonization of MRI data in MS multicenter studies
resources.note: MAGNIMS consensus recommendations for harmonizing MRI in multicentre multiple-sclerosis studies, from acquisition protocols and image analysis to data storage; useful for prospective harmonization.

resources.title: EANM/EARL harmonization strategies in PET quantification: from daily practice to multicentre oncological studies
resources.venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging
resources.note: EANM/EARL review of how to harmonize quantitative PET/CT (SUV, tumour volume, TLG) across sites, from daily quality control and accreditation to multicentre oncology trials.

resources.title: Dementia ConnEEGtome: Towards multicentric harmonization of EEG connectivity in neurodegeneration
resources.note: Reviews the sources of variability in multicentre EEG connectivity studies and gives general guidelines for harmonizing acquisition and processing protocols across sites.

resources.title: A review of harmonization strategies for quantitative PET
resources.note: Review of harmonization strategies for quantitative PET: scanner calibration and QC, protocol standardization, and post-reconstruction or feature-level harmonization.

resources.title: Challenges and Opportunities in dMRI Data Harmonization
resources.note: Book chapter laying out the open problems in diffusion MRI harmonization: where the variability comes from, what retrospective methods can and cannot fix, and how to evaluate them.

resources.title: Deep Learning in Large and Multi-Site Structural Brain MR Imaging Datasets
resources.note: Reviews deep-learning studies that pooled multi-site structural MRI and how they handled batch effects; argues that variability can help generalization but its impact must be evaluated.

resources.title: Artificial intelligence: Deep learning in oncological radiomics and challenges of interpretability and data harmonization
resources.note: Review of deep learning in oncological radiomics with a section on data harmonization across centres and scanners, alongside interpretability.

resources.title: Data harmonisation for information fusion in digital healthcare: A state-of-the-art systematic review, meta-analysis and future research directions
resources.note: Systematic review and meta-analysis of computational data harmonization in digital healthcare, with a checklist for reporting harmonization studies and flowcharts for choosing methods and metrics.

resources.title: Cross-scanner and cross-protocol diffusion MRI data harmonisation: A benchmark database and evaluation of algorithms
resources.note: Benchmark dMRI database (same subjects, three scanners with 40/80/300 mT/m gradients, standard and state-of-the-art protocols) and a comparison of five cross-scanner/protocol mapping methods.

resources.title: Cross-scanner and cross-protocol multi-shell diffusion MRI data harmonization: Algorithms and results
resources.note: Evaluation of 19 algorithms (RISH-based, deep learning, hybrid) for harmonizing multi-shell diffusion MRI across scanners and protocols on a common benchmark.

resources.title: Muti-shell Diffusion MRI Harmonisation and Enhancement Challenge (MUSHAC): Progress and Results
resources.note: Results of the Multi-shell Diffusion MRI Harmonisation and Enhancement Challenge (MUSHAC), which compared submitted harmonization and super-resolution methods.

resources.title: Comparison of traveling‐subject and ComBat harmonization methods for assessing structural brain characteristics
resources.note: Compares traveling-subject GLM, ComBat and traveling-subject ComBat on 20 participants scanned with three procedures: TS-based methods removed more measurement bias (up to 85% vs 59%), and at least 6 traveling subjects were needed.

resources.title: A multi-scanner neuroimaging data harmonization using RAVEL and ComBat
resources.note: Compares raw images, RAVEL intensity normalization, ComBat and their combination on subjects scanned at 1.5T and 3T: ComBat gave the most consistent regional harmonization; RAVEL improved intensities but added variance.

resources.title: A comparison of methods to harmonize cortical thickness measurements across scanners and sites
resources.note: Compares mixed-effects models, ComBat and ComBat-GAM on cortical thickness from 29 sites (ENIGMA-PTSD): ComBat-GAM was most sensitive to case-control and age effects.

resources.title: Validation of cross-sectional and longitudinal ComBat harmonization methods for magnetic resonance imaging data on a travelling subject cohort
resources.note: Validates neuroCombat, longCombat and gamCombat on a traveling-subject cohort (73 volunteers, 161 scans): diffusion metrics benefited, but harmonizing structural data without a scanner effect obscured real biology.

resources.title: Exploring the limits of ComBat method for multi-site diffusion MRI harmonization
resources.note: Tests the limits of ComBat on FA from 542 people at 5 sites: how well it keeps inter-subject biological variability and what happens with age-range and sample-size mismatches between sites.

resources.title: Cross-scanner reproducibility and harmonization of a diffusion MRI structural brain network: A traveling subject study of multi-b acquisition
resources.note: Traveling-subject study of cross-scanner reproducibility of diffusion-MRI structural networks (four 3T scanners), showing harmonizing at the network-matrix level reduces scanner bias while keeping subject differences.

resources.title: Impact of Preprocessing and Harmonization Methods on the Removal of Scanner Effects in Brain MRI Radiomic Features
resources.note: Compares preprocessing, six intensity normalizations and ComBat for removing scanner effects from brain-MRI radiomic features: ComBat was essential; intensity normalization alone did not remove feature-level effects.

resources.title: Intensity harmonization techniques influence radiomics features and radiomics-based predictions in sarcoma patients
resources.note: Shows that the choice of intensity harmonization (standardization, histogram matching, ComBat) changes radiomic features and predictive performance (AUROC 0.69–0.82) in sarcoma MRI.

resources.title: Impact of ComBat Harmonization on PET Radiomics-Based Tissue Classification: A Dual-Center PET/MRI and PET/CT Study
resources.note: Dual-centre PET/MR and PET/CT study: ComBat harmonization markedly improved radiomics-based tissue classification on pooled data.

resources.title: ComBat Harmonization for MRI Radiomics
resources.note: Compares ComBat with and without empirical Bayes for radiomics-based tissue classification on MRI from two vendors; both improved accuracy over unharmonized data.

resources.title: Benchmarking the generalizability of brain age models: Challenges posed by scanner variance and prediction bias
resources.note: Benchmarks how two lifespan brain-age models generalize to new youth samples, showing how scanner and protocol differences limit transfer.

resources.title: Brain‐age prediction: Systematic evaluation of site effects, and sample age range and size
resources.note: Systematic test of seven site-harmonization strategies for brain-age prediction (35,683 people): age prediction was most accurate with no site harmonization.

resources.title: Extensive Evaluation of Morphological Statistical Harmonization for Brain Age Prediction
resources.note: Evaluates three harmonization strategies for brain-age prediction on ABIDE (17 sites): similar accuracy but different sets of age-related features, a warning for interpretation.

resources.title: Removing the effects of the site in brain imaging machine-learning – Measurement and extendable benchmark
resources.note: Provides datasets and formulas to measure how well a site-removal method works for machine learning, separating removal of site effects from loss of true effects.

resources.title: Harmonized multi‐metric and multi‐centric assessment of EEG source space connectivity for dementia characterization
resources.note: Multicentre EEG pipeline (electrode-layout integration, normalization, source-space connectivity) that harmonized data across sites well enough to classify Alzheimer's disease and bvFTD.
